title: will for a decision now
rule: Use will plus the base verb for a decision you make at the moment of speaking, and for promises and offers.
ruleRu: Will и глагол без to — решение в момент речи, обещание или предложение.
exampleOk: The phone is ringing. I'll answer it.
exampleBad: The phone is ringing. I answer it.
l1Trap: Будущее передают настоящим временем, без will.

title: going to
rule: Be going to plus the base verb is a plan you already have, or something you can see is about to happen.
ruleRu: Be going to — план, который уже есть, или то, что вот-вот случится и это видно.
exampleOk: We're going to move in June.
exampleBad: We going to move in June.
l1Trap: Пропадают am/is/are: I going to.

title: will or going to
rule: Going to is a plan made before this moment. Will is a decision made now.
ruleRu: Going to — план был до разговора. Will — решение только что.
exampleOk: I forgot her birthday. I'll call her now.
exampleBad: I forgot her birthday. I'm going to call her now, I just decided.
l1Trap: Оба переводятся «буду», и will ставят на заранее купленные планы.

title: present continuous for plans
rule: A fixed arrangement, often with a time, uses the present continuous. I'm meeting the dentist at four.
ruleRu: Уже назначенная встреча — present continuous. I'm meeting the dentist at four.
exampleOk: We're having dinner with them on Saturday.
exampleBad: We have dinner with them on Saturday.
l1Trap: Будущую договорённость ставят в present simple.

title: present after when, if, before
rule: After when, if, before, after, until and as soon as, use the present simple for the future, not will.
ruleRu: После when, if, before, until будущее выражают present simple. I'll call you when I arrive.
exampleOk: If it rains, we'll stay in.
exampleBad: If it will rain, we stay in.
l1Trap: Will ставят в обе части, потому что по-русски будущее в обеих.

title: can for ability
rule: Can plus the base verb means ability now. There is no to and no -s. The past is could.
ruleRu: Can и глагол без to и без -s — умение сейчас. Прошлое — could.
exampleOk: He can drive, but he couldn't last year.
exampleBad: He can to drive, but he caned last year.
l1Trap: После can ставят to или -s.

title: could you
rule: Could you plus the base verb is a polite request. Could here is not the past.
ruleRu: Could you и глагол — вежливая просьба, не прошедшее время.
exampleOk: Could you say that again, please?
exampleBad: Could you to say that again?
l1Trap: Could воспринимают только как прошлое от can, либо ставят to.

title: must and have to
rule: Both mean it is necessary. Must is often the speaker's own rule. Have to is a rule from outside. There is no to after must.
ruleRu: Оба значат «нужно». Must чаще своё «я так считаю». Have to — внешнее правило. После must нет to.
exampleOk: You have to wear a helmet on the site.
exampleBad: You must to wear a helmet on the site.
l1Trap: После must ставят to.

title: mustn't and don't have to
rule: Mustn't means it is forbidden. Don't have to means it is not necessary.
ruleRu: Mustn't — нельзя. Don't have to — не обязательно.
exampleOk: You don't have to pay. It's free. You mustn't park here.
exampleBad: You mustn't pay. It's free.
l1Trap: Оба переводят «не нужно», и запрет путают с отсутствием обязанности.

title: should
rule: Should plus the base verb is advice, not a hard order. There is no to. The negative is shouldn't.
ruleRu: Should и глагол без to — совет, не приказ. Отрицание — shouldn't.
exampleOk: You should sleep more.
exampleBad: You should to sleep more.
l1Trap: После should ставят to.

title: may and might
rule: May and might plus the base verb mean something is possible. Maybe is an adverb, one word: Maybe it will rain.
ruleRu: May и might — «возможно». Maybe — отдельное слово-наречие, не глагол.
exampleOk: I might be late.
exampleBad: I may to be late.
l1Trap: Maybe и may be смешивают, и после may ставят to.

title: would like
rule: Would like is a polite want. It takes to plus the base verb, or a noun. I'd like a coffee. Not I like to when you are ordering.
ruleRu: Would like — вежливое «хочу». Дальше to и глагол или существительное.
exampleOk: I'd like to book a table.
exampleBad: I like to book a table, please.
l1Trap: Would теряют, и просьба становится «мне нравится».

title: should have
rule: Should have plus the past participle is advice or regret about the past. You should have told me. It means you didn't.
ruleRu: Should have и третья форма — «надо было» про прошлое. Это значит, что не сделали.
exampleOk: I should have left earlier.
exampleBad: I should left earlier.
l1Trap: Have пропускают: should told, should went.

title: must have
titleRu: Must have — наверняка так и было
rule: Must have plus the past participle is a strong guess about the past. It does not mean the person was obliged.
ruleRu: Must have и третья форма — уверенная догадка о прошлом, не обязанность.
exampleOk: The lights are off. They must have gone home.
exampleBad: The lights are off. They must went home.
l1Trap: Must have понимают как «должен был» и строят must went.

title: zero conditional
rule: For facts that are always true, use the present simple in both parts. If you heat ice, it melts.
ruleRu: Для того, что верно всегда, в обеих частях present simple.
exampleOk: If water reaches 100 degrees, it boils.
exampleBad: If water will reach 100 degrees, it boil.
l1Trap: В if ставят will даже для закона природы.

title: first conditional
rule: A real future possibility: if plus present simple, and will in the other part. Not if plus will.
ruleRu: Реальное будущее: if и present simple, в другой части will.
exampleOk: If you hurry, you will catch the bus.
exampleBad: If you will hurry, you catch the bus.
l1Trap: Will оказывается в части с if.

title: second conditional
rule: An unreal present: if plus past simple, and would plus the base verb. If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
ruleRu: Нереальное сейчас: if и past simple, дальше would и глагол.
exampleOk: If I knew her number, I would call.
exampleBad: If I would know her number, I called.
l1Trap: Would ставят в обе части: If I would know.

title: If I were
titleRu: If I were, не If I was
rule: In unreal if-clauses, were is the usual form for every person, including I. If I were you.
ruleRu: В нереальном if форма were для всех, включая I. If I were rich.
exampleOk: If I were you, I would apologise.
exampleBad: If I was you, I will apologise.
l1Trap: Ставят was и will вместо were и would.

title: third conditional
titleRu: Третий тип: прошлое, которого не было
rule: An unreal past: if plus past perfect, and would have plus the past participle. It did not happen.
ruleRu: Нереальное прошлое: if и past perfect, дальше would have и третья форма.
exampleOk: If we had booked, we would have got a table.
exampleBad: If we would have booked, we got a table.
l1Trap: Would have ставят в часть с if, а had теряют.

title: unless
rule: Unless means if not. It is already negative, so do not add another not.
ruleRu: Unless значит if not и уже содержит отрицание. Второе not не нужно.
exampleOk: Don't call unless it's urgent.
exampleBad: Don't call unless it isn't urgent.
l1Trap: Unless переводят как «если» и добавляют не.

title: wish about now
rule: Wish about a present fact takes the past simple. I wish I knew. It means I don't know.
ruleRu: Wish о настоящем факте требует past simple. I wish I knew — «жаль, что не знаю».
exampleOk: I wish I lived closer.
exampleBad: I wish I live closer.
l1Trap: После wish оставляют настоящее время.

title: wish about the past
rule: Wish about the past takes the past perfect. I wish I had studied. It means I didn't.
ruleRu: Wish о прошлом — past perfect. I wish I had studied.
exampleOk: I wish I hadn't said that.
exampleBad: I wish I didn't said that.
l1Trap: Для сожаления о прошлом had пропадает.
